In 2021, Kraft saw the Revolution set an MLS record with 73 regular season points en route to the club’s first Supporters’ Shield title. In December 2019, Kraft unveiled a state-of-the-art training center for the Revolution situated on 68 acres in Foxborough adjacent to Gillette Stadium, providing his soccer club with a world-class home that stands among the world’s best soccer training facilities.
The United States Men’s and Women’s National Teams have also enjoyed tremendous support from the Kraft family and soccer fans throughout New England. Since 1990, Foxborough has hosted 33 international matches involving U.S. national teams at Foxboro Stadium (1990-2001) and Gillette Stadium (2002-present). No team in the Modern Era has more wins (47) and advances (51) than the Fire. The closest teams to that wins mark are the Seattle Sounders FC, FC Dallas, and the now-defunct Rochester Rhinos with 39.
Chicago Fire players celebrate after scoring a goal against Detroit City FC in the Fourth Round of the 2025 US Open Cup. Photo: Chicago Fire FC
In league play, they’ve been far less successful. After winning the MLS Cup in their debut year of 1998, the only other accolade the Fire has earned was the Supporters’ Shield in 2003. The club was on a dreadful seven-season run of missing the MLS Cup playoffs from 2018-2024 before snapping that streak last year.
The Windy City is home to four other Open Cup champions besides the Fire. Teams such as Bricklayers FC, Sparta A & BA, Croatian SC, and AAC Eagles, among many others, ensured that a Chicago team was a contender for the crown. Prior to the Fire lifting the trophy for the first time in 1998, the last Illinois-based club to win the Open Cup was the AAC Eagles in 1990.

Our 25 Year Journey
FC Platinum, called Mimosa Football Club then, was formed on the 1st of July 1995 as a social club to entertain Mimosa Mining Company employees residing at the mine. The team was promoted to Division 2, enduring a two-year stint before promotion to Division 1. It faced subsequent relegation in the same year. The team finally regained its division 1 status in 2004 after 4 years under the guidance of coach Luke Petros and John Phiri. The team continued to work tirelessly and got promoted to the highest local football league in 2011 under the leadership of Jairos Tapera. In the very same year the team’s title was changed to its now affectionally known name, FC Platinum. In 2014 the platinum side sponsorship was wholly taken over by FC Platinum Holdings up to this date.

**American Football Canterbury**originally started in **2010** as a university social club under the banner of **‘GridironSoc’**, transitioning to **‘University of Canterbury American Football’** in **2011**. Created by founding father **Jono Entwistle**, it began with a group of
likeminded students hosting weekly **flag football** games on**I****lam Fields** at the **University of Canterbury**. The rules and games were rough to say the least, but as interest grew, so did the sport itself, leading to the creation of new teams and various competitions being staged.
The **2012-2013** seasons witnessed substantial change, with the establishment of **American Football Canterbury Inc**, led by stalwarts**Brad Cottam** and **Mase Shaw**. During these seasons **full contact football** was also introduced. After many months of fundraising, **AFC** was able to purchase some old pads and helmets from the States and enlisted a local **ex-NCAA Division 1 College** and **Arena Football League** coach to help teach them the sport.
A **5-a-side** version of **contact football** was adopted. Adapted from **7-a-side** football, it allowed for shorter, enjoyable games to be played by less numbers. Ideal for a programme in its infancy.
**2014**signalled the un-official beginning of the coveted **AFC Championship** with foundation teams, the **Warhawks** and **Rebels** competing in the inaugural season.
However, **2015** is considered the first “official” season of the **AFC Championship**, with the introduction of another cornerstone team, the **Wolfpack**, joining the original two teams to create a three-team championship.
In **2016**, **AFC** moved from its original home at **Ilam Fields** to its new headquarters at **Te Kahu Park** in **Wigram**, after a brief stint at **Addington Park**.

**2016** also saw **AFC** turn its attention to promoting the sport to a younger audience. Firstly, by establishing **AFC**’s first **American Football** camp for kids run by **Coach****Mase Shaw** during the school holidays. From this camp, two teams were selected to play in the first ever **Junior flag football** game between the **Junior Pack** and the **Junior Hawks**. The two teams meeting in the curtain raiser to the **2016 AFC Championship** game.
The following year, **Junior** player numbers grew exponentially, resulting in the creation of New Zealand’s first ever **Junior flag football** competition. This initial 10-team competition set the platform for the extremely popular **Canterbury Junior Flag Football Championship** that is played today by an ever-increasing number of **Junior** players.
​**AFC** further expanded in **2019**. This time **Coach Shaw** introduced a **full contact****Youth** programme for teenagers. Our 25 Year Journey
FC Platinum, called Mimosa Football Club then, was formed on the 1st of July 1995 as a social club to entertain Mimosa Mining Company employees residing at the mine. The team was promoted to Division 2, enduring a two-year stint before promotion to Division 1. It faced subsequent relegation in the same year. The team finally regained its division 1 status in 2004 after 4 years under the guidance of coach Luke Petros and John Phiri. The team continued to work tirelessly and got promoted to the highest local football league in 2011 under the leadership of Jairos Tapera. In the very same year the team’s title was changed to its now affectionally known name, FC Platinum. In 2014 the platinum side sponsorship was wholly taken over by FC Platinum Holdings up to this date.
